Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then details and next steps below.

TL;DR: We support both soft-throttle (grace) and hard-cap (freeze). By default hosted customers are on a soft-throttle behavior with tiered notifications; hard-cap must be enabled by the customer or requested in a contract amendment. Emergency one-time buffers/credits are handled manually by Sales/Finance and require approvals.

Details:
- Default (soft-throttle): when spend projection crosses your monthly threshold we start to degrade non-essential routing (lower-cost model variants), reduce batch sizes, and apply token-rate throttles to hold latency SLOs where possible. Calls continue to return responses but you may see increased latency/shorter responses.
- Hard-cap (freeze): when enabled, requests that would push you over the cap return 402/429-like errors with a short message explaining the cap. No tokens are billed beyond the cap. This is the recommended setting if you need strict budget enforcement.
- Notifications: we send email + console banner, and can enable webhook callbacks to a customer URL. We also have an optional pager/SMS integration (Enterprise add-on).
- Emergency buffer/credits: Sales can authorize a temporary buffer (one-time uplift) or apply a credit while a contract amendment is routed. This is manual and typically takes ~24–72 hours depending on approvals and legal review.

Operational next steps I recommend:
1) If you want hard enforcement, confirm the dollar cap and we'll flip the cap in the account settings and add a webhook to finance@skycraft.ai.
2) If you'd prefer a soft window (30% overrun grace) we can set that policy and provide a daily spend digest.
3) If you need a short-term uplift today, let us know the amount and we can route a one-time buffer request to Finance (cc Markus).

I've attached a short runbook link and will follow up with sample policy text your procurement team can include in an amendment.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Looping in some finance / legal-friendly language. For customer amendments we use the following options in SOWs/Amendments:

- Option A (Hard Cap): "Customer may elect a hard spend cap. Once the cap is reached, Redwood will block additional consumption. No additional charges will be incurred without prior written authorization."
- Option B (Soft Throttle + Alerts): "Customer may elect soft-throttle behavior where Redwood will continue serving requests but reserve the right to reduce throughput or route to compatible model variants to limit spend. Redwood will provide 24-hour and 6-hour alerts before projected cap."
- Option C (Buffer Credit): "Temporary buffer up to $X may be granted at Redwood's discretion; customer acknowledges that buffer is one-time and may require subsequent billing reconciliation."

If Sales needs a same-day buffer, we can approve up to $5k with a finance sign-off from me. Anything above requires VP approval.

-Markus
Director of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
